title: In weakness and fear (1 Corinthians 2)
hookLine: Paul came to them trembling, not with clever speeches
tomorrow: two teachers, one church. who gets credit for the growth?

lines: WHAT DID HE DECIDE TO SAY?
cards: Shaking hands before a recital, a speech, a first day somewhere new. Paul had them too. Here's how he remembers walking into Corinth: "And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling."
No grand entrance. The man some of them now chant like a team name came to their city nervous. So what did a trembling man decide to say?

teach.b: First, what he didn't bring: "And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom".
Then what he chose: "For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified."
One subject, on purpose. "And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man's wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power". Why come that way?

teach.h: FAITH THAT DOESN'T LEAN ON HIM.
teach.b: "That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God." If a great talker had won them over, their faith would lean on the talker: the fan-club problem, solved before it started.

teach.h: EYE HATH NOT SEEN, BUT REVEALED.
teach.b: Later in the chapter comes a line some readers lift out on its own: "Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him."
Heard alone, it can sound like heaven someday, hidden for now. But Paul's next words are: "But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit."
The nervous man with plain words isn't hiding anything. He's saying the depth comes from God, not from the speaker.

how: Some preachers and teachers read 1 Corinthians 2:1–5 before they speak, as a reminder to keep their words plain and point beyond themselves.

games.q: what does “in weakness and fear” mean?
o: how the disciples hid after the crucifixion
how Paul says he first came to Corinth
how Peter felt on the night he denied Jesus

games.q: how Paul came to Corinth — tap the pairs.

s: Paul says he arrived in Corinth with a polished speech
he came not with excellency of speech, in weakness and much trembling.
'eye hath not seen' is followed by 'God hath revealed them'
the next line: but God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit.
Paul wanted their faith to rest on a great speaker
not in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.

games.q: you're giving a toast at your brother's graduation. you have a clever line and a true one, and you're nervous. what fits 1 Corinthians 2?
o: say the true one plainly, nerves and all.
use the clever line so nobody notices the nerves.
skip the toast until you can do it without shaking.
games.why: Paul came trembling, chose one subject, and kept his speech plain, so what he said wouldn't lean on how he said it.

practice: Write down one thing you need to say soon: a thank-you, an apology, a hard truth. Cross out every word that's there to impress until only the plain sentence is left. Then sit with it, shaky or not.

wordCard.voice: In weakness and fear. How Paul says he first came to Corinth: trembling, plain-spoken, with one subject.

orig.note: Greek: weakness. In 1 Corinthians 2:3: in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.

carryVoice: The line to keep: in weakness and much trembling, and the message still got through. Go gently.
